fin_q_001.note: Simple single-sentence lookup; fine as an easy item for the policy/APM topic.

fin_q_002.note: Key fact '5.9%' doesn't check the direction; require 'decline/down' (or -5.9%) so that a '+5.9%' answer fails.

fin_q_003.note: Plausible net-debt component lookup with a look-alike table trap; the trio of items is slightly arbitrary.

fin_q_004.note: question_natural asks only for the total, but the key facts also require 2,715 and 719, so a correct natural answer (3,200) would fail. Ask for the components in the natural version too.

fin_q_005.note: Same business unit, page area and year as fin_q_002 but a different metric; acceptable. Units trap (€ vs tons/TEU) is good.

fin_q_007.note: Core leverage KPIs. The 2025 equity ratio and net gearing values duplicate fin_q_017.

fin_q_008.note: The two changes have opposite signs (-4.5% FY, +42.9% Q4), but the key facts carry bare percentages. Add direction (decline/increase) to the key facts.

fin_q_009.note: Mechanical % change on the same two net-debt figures that fin_q_013 already tests (and fin_q_007's answer repeats). Replace with a calculation analysts actually need (e.g. net debt/EBITDA or net debt excl. leases).

fin_q_010.note: Good header/column trap (full year vs Q4, Group column). The share is a somewhat unusual but defensible metric.

fin_q_011.note: Routine ETR derivation; the sign convention of the tax line is a mild trap.

fin_q_012.note: Strong multi-page item. The natural version's singular 'which division' slightly hints there is only one; the key facts don't penalise extra (wrong) divisions being listed.

fin_q_013.note: The question text is convoluted (a parenthetical about which liabilities measure); simplify the canonical wording. It overlaps fin_q_009 on the net-debt change.

fin_q_014.note: Restatement check is auditor-relevant, but the €1m rounding difference has little decision value; it is kept for its look-alike-value trap.

fin_q_015.note: Good multi-document trend item; the cumulative figure is labelled as a decline, so the sign is covered.

fin_q_016.note: Three-part definitional question; 'how it relates' is vague. Key facts are loose (a bare 'dividends'; one fact bundles the formula and the 2026 change into a single string); split them into a precise formula and the 2026 replacement.

fin_q_017.note: The definition key fact 'total assets' is loose on its own, but the paired numeric facts protect it. The 2025 values duplicate fin_q_007.

fin_q_018.note: Valid abstention item (the financial calendar mentions a Q1 date, which is a nice distractor).

fin_q_019.note: The question says the NBB 'set' the requirements, but the source says they are SRB MREL instructions notified by the NBB. Reword, and shorten the over-specified question.

fin_q_020.note: 'Highest proportion of collateral used by an issuer' is an opaque phrase that copies the report's wording, and few users would ask for it. The bare '6%' key fact is too loose; reframe it as single-issuer collateral concentration vs Tier 1 and tie '6%' to Tier 1 in the key fact.

fin_q_022.note: The basis caveats (CRR3 vs CRR2) make it read like a test item, but it is needed for clarity and the header trap is meaningful.

fin_q_023.note: Good IRRBB item. It partly overlaps fin_q_068 (same LUKB EVE table). Key facts drop the minus sign, but 'negative change' is in the fact label.

fin_q_025.note: question_natural's 'what drove it' invites narrative drivers (CRR3, profits) rather than the CET1 capital and TREA amounts that the key facts require. Ask explicitly for CET1 capital and TREA.

fin_q_026.note: Recomputing a ratio that is printed next to its inputs is a test artefact (same pattern as fin_q_027 and fin_q_126); the natural version still says 'recomputed'. Ask instead for the leverage ratio and its headroom over the 3% minimum.

fin_q_027.note: Recompute-the-reported-ratio pattern (also fin_q_026 and fin_q_126); the EUR-thousands trap is the only value, and the natural version still says 'recomputed'. Ask instead for CET1 headroom over the requirement, using the thousands units.

fin_q_028.note: Core capital question. The reference answer's mix of pro forma and originally reported 2024 ratios is useful context, but the key facts don't test it.

fin_q_029.note: Cross-jurisdiction CET1 comparison of unrelated banks is unusual for a real user, but it is a fair multi-document entity-disambiguation test. The ASN figure duplicates fin_q_025.

fin_q_030.note: It compares a point-in-time LCR with a Q4 monthly average, so the analytical comparison is weak. The natural version drops 'key metrics table' and becomes ambiguous (LUKB discloses several LCR figures). Pin the LUKB basis in both versions or drop the item.

fin_q_031.note: Valid abstention item. It follows the same pattern as fin_q_018 and fin_q_082, so the set doesn't need more of these.

fin_q_032.note: Niche (central-bank risk) but well defined. The reference correctly notes there is no exact 2024 figure.

fin_q_033.note: Core KPI but a trivial lookup. The 201% also appears in fin_q_041 and fin_q_078.
